title: Learning Biological Hierarchies in Single-Cell Foundation Models
claim: A model is built from a data corpus, structure-derived distance supervision and tailored losses, then evaluated across diverse downstream tasks.
layout: 4 panels: three across top, task strip below, left-to-right
description: A wide multi-panel figure. Panel (a), top left, shows the CZ CELLxGENE logo with an arrow into a database cylinder labeled Pretrain Data Corpus. The cylinder lists 27.5 million cells, 210 tissues and 566 cell types. Beside it is a circular sunburst chart of tissue and disease proportions, with tissue labels around the rim and a disease color legend underneath. Panel (b), top middle, shows a cell-type ontology tree with depth levels 0 to 3. Arrows lead from the tree to a blue-red LCA distance heatmap with a Far to Close color bar. Panel (c), top right, shows the dynamic margin ranking loss with an anchor, positive and negative on a dashed arc, plus the alignment loss equation and two matched heatmaps. Panel (d), bottom, is a row of four rounded boxes with blue headers: cell type annotation, novel cell identification, gene function prediction and spatial gene imputation. Each holds a small icon-based schematic.
caption: Proposed model workflow. (a) scOntoFM pre-training data corpus details (left), and the distribution of major tissues and diseases in the corpus (right). (b) An illustration of cell ontology graph and its derived LCA distance matrix. (c) Ontology-aware loss terms in scOntoFM, the dynamic margin $\alpha(c_a,c_n)$ is controlled by the distance between the anchor cell-type $c_a$ and negative cell-type $c_n$, and the depth of the anchor $c_a$ in the ontology graph. Down below is the hierarchical ontology alignment loss, in which $\Delta^{emb}$ and $ \tilde{\Delta}^{onto} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times B}$ represent correspondingly the distance matrix of our model embeddings and its corresponding LCA distance matrix in the batch (of size $B$), and where $r_n^{emb}$ and $r_n^{onto}$ are the soft-ranking rows in their respective distance matrices. $\rho_S(\cdot, \cdot)$ is the Spearman correlation for the soft-ranking vectors. (d) Downstream tasks of scOntoFM, from left to right and grouped into cell- and gene-level tasks as presented in the results.
abstract: Cell types are organized by taxonomic relationships that define lineages in the so-called cell ontology. However, most existing foundation models typically ignore cell-type lineages encoded in this cell ontology. We introduce a biologically informed foundation model called scOntoFM, which embeds hierarchical cell ontology into representation learning. Using Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA) distances from the ontology graph, our framework pairs efficient offline triplet sampling with hierarchical cell-ontology learning. This approach jointly preserves local neighborhoods and shapes the global embedding geometry to reflect the ontology structure. Across diverse cell- and gene-level benchmarks, the model consistently improves performance, with especially strong gains in zero-shot settings. Our model also balances batch integration with biological structure preservation, providing complementary perspectives to existing embedding evaluation frameworks and supporting scalable biological discovery.
